target.title: fix(ci): enforce plugin SDK API baseline
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a clean-`main` failure where the Plugin SDK API contract check reported drift after intended public exports landed, while ordinary PR CI did not run the check. Unrelated source PRs could therefore discover a broken baseline in changed-gates even though their exact-head CI stayed green.

## Why This Change Was Made

#111149 intentionally exposed the agent-harness session-fork contracts and the session-catalog upstream-link write/delete helpers, but commit `ea54060223134c103ce396f914c735b707f7c4b2` did not regenerate the API contract manifest. A later concurrent refresh in #111249 repaired other inherited entries but left `session-catalog` stale and carried a non-current `agent-harness-runtime` hash.

While this repair was in review, #111142 merged commit `58452de711884d4dbfd4c7899c2bc597e5bb524e`, intentionally retiring dead config keys and deduplicating channel schemas. That changed the generated declarations for `bundled-channel-config-schema`, `channel-config-primitives`, `channel-config-schema`, `channel-config-schema-legacy`, `compat`, `config-contracts`, `config-schema`, `config-types`, `discord`, `provider-stream-shared`, and `telegram-account` without refreshing this manifest. These are intended surface reductions and shared-schema type changes from the already-landed config refactor, not accidental new exports.

Commit `f07a1fb5027f6af7cacb360968085e224d094eae` later refreshed the generated manifest on `main` while this PR was under review. Rebasing therefore dropped this PR's identical manifest repair as already upstream. The durable missing piece remains CI prevention.

This change adds a fail-closed `check-plugin-sdk-api-baseline` shard to ordinary full Node CI. The existing changed-gate scope remains intentionally broad because transitive production-source changes can alter public declarations.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. Plugin SDK contributors now get the same API-contract enforcement in hosted CI that changed-gates already apply locally, so baseline drift cannot silently reach `main`.

## Evidence

- Clean-main reproduction: `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check` failed with `Manifest mismatch: docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` ([Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29678244358)).
- Generated declaration comparison isolated the original intended additions to `agent-harness-runtime` and `session-catalog`; the refreshed manifest passed after the first rebase ([Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29678696105)).
- After #111142 merged, the newly added CI shard immediately caught its additional config-surface drift on this PR ([CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29679479004)). The manifest was regenerated again and checked against that refactor's source changes before update.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- .github/workflows/ci.yml docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256 test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts` passed, including formatting, API baseline generation, test-root types, and script lint ([Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29679905549)).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts`: 86 passed, 1 skipped.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`: 353 entrypoints / 8,601 exports, within the current budget ([Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29678614486)).
- Autoreview: clean after replacing the initial missing-script skip with fail-closed execution, and clean again after the latest rebase reduced the PR to its two-file prevention patch.

AI-assisted; the implementation and generated declaration changes were reviewed against the owning SDK barrels, their callers/callees, the config-surface refactor, and the upstream Codex thread/fork contract.
